1: While staying at Jetavana, the Buddha told this story about Vāsabhakhattiyā.
2:
Vāsabhakhattiyā was the daughter of Mahānāma the Sakyan, born of a slave woman named Nāgamuṇḍā.
She became chief queen of the King of Kosala and bore him a son.
3:
But when the king later learned she was a slave woman's daughter, he took away her rank,
and that of her son Viṭaṭūbha too. The two of them lived shut away inside the palace.
4:
Knowing this, the Buddha went to the palace one forenoon with five hundred monks and sat on the seat prepared.
“Great king, where is Vāsabhakhattiyā?” The king told him what had happened.
5:
“Great king, whose daughter is Vāsabhakhattiyā?” “Mahānāma’s, Venerable Sir.”
“And to whom did she come as a bride?” “To me, Venerable Sir.”
6:
“Great king, she is a king’s daughter, she came to a king, and she bore a son to a king.
For what reason should that son not own his father’s kingdom?
7:
Kings of old gave their kingdom even to a son born of a firewood woman they met but for a moment.”
The king asked him to tell that story, and the Blessed One revealed what was hidden by rebirth.
8:
Long ago, King Brahmadatta of Bārāṇasī went to his pleasure-park with a great retinue,
wandering about, eager for flowers and fruit.
9:
In a grove of the park he saw a woman gathering firewood as she sang.
His heart was drawn to her, and he lived with her.
10:
At that very moment the Bodhisatta was conceived in her womb, which grew heavy as if filled with diamond.
“Sire, a child has been conceived in me,” she said.
11:
The king gave her his signet ring: “If it is a daughter, spend this to raise her;
if it is a son, bring him to me with this ring.” Then he went away.
12: When her time came, she gave birth to the Bodhisatta.
13: When he was old enough to run about the playground, the children would say, “We’ve been hit by a fatherless boy!”
14:
Hearing this, the Bodhisatta went to his mother. “Mother, who is my father?”
“My dear, you are the son of the King of Bārāṇasī.”
15:
“Mother, is there any witness?” She told him what the king had said when he gave her the ring.
“Then why don’t you take me to my father?”
16: Understanding her son’s wish, she went to the palace gate and had herself announced to the king.
17:
Summoned inside, she paid homage: “Sire, this is your son.”
The king knew it, yet ashamed before the assembly he said, “He is not my son.”
18: “Sire, here is your ring. Do you recognize it?” “This is not my ring either.”
19:
“Sire, now I have no witness except an act of truth. If this child was born of you,
may he stay in the air; if not, may he fall to the ground and die.”
20: Then she seized the Bodhisatta by the feet and threw him up into the air.
21: Sitting cross-legged in the air, the Bodhisatta taught his father the Dhamma in a sweet voice and spoke this verse:
22:
“I am your son, great king; O lord of men, raise me.
The king supports many others — why not his own child?”
23:
“Come, my son!” said the king, stretching out his hand,
and a thousand hands stretched out with him: “I will raise him! I will raise him!”
24: The Bodhisatta came down into no other hands but the king’s, and sat on his lap.
25: The king made him viceroy and made his mother chief queen.
26: After his father’s death he became King Kaṭṭhavāhana, ruled righteously, and passed on according to his deeds.
27:
The Buddha gave this teaching to the King of Kosala and linked the two stories:
“The mother then was Mahāmāyā, the father King Suddhodana, and King Kaṭṭhavāhana was I myself.”
